# Parameters and Selection Definitions

Parameters carry reactive values between components. Selection definitions
combine selection clauses and connect views. JSON/YAML specifications declare
these objects under `params` and use `$name` to refer to them.

JavaScript `vg.Param` and `vg.Selection` are the existing core constructors.
Their identities and live event behavior are preserved. See the
[Param runtime API](/api/core/param) and [Selection runtime API](/api/core/selection)
for updates, clauses, and listeners. Python `vg.param(...)` and
`vg.selection.*(...)` build serializable definitions; they do not create
JavaScript runtime instances.

## References

`$value` refers to a named parameter, while `$$column` denotes a parameter
whose value supplies a column name. The TypeScript `ParamRef` type requires
the dollar prefix. Its existing wire-schema definition admits any string;
runtime resolution still requires the reference syntax.

An array parameter resolves its parameter elements by identity. A scalar
parameter containing the string `"$name"` keeps that literal string. The
array starter demonstrates a named upstream value and a dependent domain.

## Python authoring

`vg.param(value=None)` preserves explicit null. Lists create array parameters;
other values create scalar parameters. Native Python dates serialize as ISO
date strings inside a `date` definition. Selection factories accept arbitrary
keyword options, omit `None`, preserve falsy values, and resolve nested
parameter objects when the containing specification is serialized.

Use `params={...}` to choose names explicitly. `Spec` assigns unused names
such as `_param0` to inline objects, while `View` and `vg.spec(...)` can
discover parameter names in the caller's local variables. The
<a :href="withBase('/templates/params/anonymous.py')" download>anonymous Python starter</a>
shows inline naming. It is Python-only: JSON/YAML definitions already have
explicit names and JavaScript holds live objects directly.

## Selection factories

| JavaScript | Python | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Selection.intersect(options)` | `selection.intersect(**opts)` | Create a selection that intersects clauses. |
| `Selection.crossfilter(options)` | `selection.crossfilter(**opts)` | Create a cross-filtered intersection selection. |
| `Selection.union(options)` | `selection.union(**opts)` | Create a selection that unions clauses. |
| `Selection.single(options)` | `selection.single(**opts)` | Create a selection that retains a single clause. |

JavaScript `Selection.crossfilter(...)` forces cross-filtering on, including
when `cross: false` was supplied. Declarative and Python definitions retain
the specified `cross` value until the JavaScript runtime constructs the
selection. The `ParamDate` wire contract accepts any string without date-format
validation; use ISO dates for executable examples.

## ParamRef

A parameter reference written as a dollar sign followed by its name.

```ts
export type ParamRef = `$${string}`;
```

## ParamBase

Base properties shared by Param definitions.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `'value'` | false | The type of reactive parameter. One of: - `"value"` (default) for a standard `Param` - `"intersect"` for a `Selection` that intersects clauses (logical "and") - `"union"` for a `Selection` that unions clauses (logical "or") - `"single"` for a `Selection` that retains a single clause only - `"crossfilter"` for a cross-filtered intersection `Selection` |

## Param

A Param definition.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `ParamValue` | true | The initial parameter value. |

Extends `ParamBase`.

## ParamDate

A Date-valued Param definition.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | `string` | true | The initial parameter value as an ISO date/time string to be parsed to a Date object. |

Extends `ParamBase`.

## ParamLiteral

Literal Param values.

```ts
export type ParamLiteral = null | string | number | boolean;
```

## ParamValue

Valid Param values.

```ts
export type ParamValue = ParamLiteral | Array<ParamLiteral | ParamRef>;
```

## Selection

A Selection definition.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `select` | `'crossfilter' \| 'intersect' \| 'single' \| 'union'` | true | The type of reactive parameter. One of: - `"value"` (default) for a standard `Param` - `"intersect"` for a `Selection` that intersects clauses (logical "and") - `"union"` for a `Selection` that unions clauses (logical "or") - `"single"` for a `Selection` that retains a single clause only - `"crossfilter"` for a cross-filtered intersection `Selection` |
| `cross` | `boolean` | false | A flag for cross-filtering, where selections made in a plot filter others but not oneself (default `false`, except for `crossfilter` selections). |
| `empty` | `boolean` | false | A flag for setting an initial empty selection state. If true, a selection with no clauses corresponds to an empty selection with no records. If false, a selection with no clauses selects all values. |
| `include` | `ParamRef \| Array<ParamRef>` | false | Upstream selections whose clauses should be included as part of this selection. Any clauses or activations published to the upstream selections will be relayed to this selection. |

## ParamDefinition

A Param or Selection definition.

```ts
export type ParamDefinition = ParamValue | Param | ParamDate | Selection;
```


## Coordinated-view starters

Each starter creates two plots backed by a small inline SQL table. Value
parameters supply a mark channel or domain to both plots; selection starters
attach a toggle to the first plot and filter the coordinated views. Click a
point to select its x value. Cross-filtering keeps the originating plot visible.

| Variant | Downloads |
| --- | --- |
| `crossfilter` | [YAML](/templates/params/crossfilter.yaml), [JSON](/templates/params/crossfilter.json), [JavaScript](/templates/params/crossfilter.js), <a :href="withBase('/templates/params/crossfilter.py')" download>Python</a> |
